# entire-rsl

`entire rsl` shows what a repository's [gittuf](https://gittuf.dev) Reference
State Log (RSL) records for a branch, tag or Entire checkpoint: who pushed it,
when, and whether gittuf verification passes. It is a plugin for the
[Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) and also runs standalone as
`entire-rsl`.

entire-rsl is read-only, with exceptions that only touch gittuf refs:
`entire rsl refresh`, `--fetch`, and fetching a missing RSL when you agree to
it.

## Install

From a release, once published:

```sh
entire plugin install rsl
```

From a local build:

```sh
mise run build
entire plugin install ./bin/entire-rsl
```

## Quickstart

### 1. Create a repository on Entire

Follow the [Entire quickstart](https://docs.entire.com/quickstart) to install
the Entire CLI,
[create a repository on Entire](https://docs.entire.com/quickstart#create-a-new-repository-on-entire),
clone it and
[enable Entire](https://docs.entire.com/quickstart#2-open-a-repository-and-enable-entire)
in it. Then install entire-rsl (see [Install](#install)) and run the commands
below from the repository root.

### 2. Fetch the RSL

A new repository already has a policy and a first RSL entry. `refresh` fetches
them from `origin`, or from the remote you name:


I've updated the Install section of `README.md`. Despite the heading you mentioned, the text lives under **Install**, and the **Quickstart** section below it just links to it. Nothing is committed.

- **Using the plugin system:** replaces "From a release, once published:" and runs `entire plugin index update` before `entire plugin install rsl`.
- **Directly from a release:** set `VERSION`/`OS`/`ARCH`, then it downloads the archive and `checksums.txt`, checks the archive with `sha256sum --check` (`shasum -a 256 --check` on macOS), extracts `entire-rsl` and copies it into `~/.local/bin`. A note covers Windows, where the archive is a `.zip`.

I ran the checksum and extract steps against the local snapshot in `dist/`. The check printed `OK` and the archive holds only `entire-rsl`. The download step is untested because no release or tag exists yet.

Decisions for you:

- **Copy, not `entire plugin install`:** for the direct install I copy the binary onto `PATH`. `entire plugin install ./entire-rsl` only creates a symlink, so the plugin would break once someone deletes the extracted file. The README says this too.
- **Tag format:** the download URL assumes tags look like `v0.1.0` and that releases are on GitHub. If tags won't have the `v`, the `BASE` line needs changing.
- **What the check proves:** it only catches a corrupted download, not a tampered one. `checksums.txt` comes from the same release, so anyone who can change the archive can change it too. If you want a real authenticity check, the release would need signatures or GitHub build attestations (for example, verified with `gh attestation verify`). Nothing like that exists yet: there is no release workflow, and goreleaser only builds by hand as a draft.

**README:** a failed check now stops the direct install. The block runs inside `( set -euo pipefail ... )`, so the first failed step stops it before `tar` and `install`. I tested the README block in both bash and zsh with `v0.0.1-rc.2`:

I also moved the "use `shasum -a 256 --check` on macOS" note out of the code block into the text below it. In a default zsh, a trailing `#` in pasted commands isn't a comment, so the note would have been passed to `sha256sum` as arguments.

**RSL warning:** after any fetch of the gittuf refs (`refresh`, `--fetch`, or the prompt when there's no local RSL), entire-rsl warns on stderr if `refs/gittuf/reference-state-log` or `refs/gittuf/policy` didn't come back:

```
Warning: origin has no refs/gittuf/reference-state-log or refs/gittuf/policy. RSL may not be enabled for the repository, or origin may not be hosted on Entire.
```

If only one ref is missing, the message names just that one. The check lives in the shared `a.syncGittufRefs` in `cmd/entire-rsl/cli/repo.go`, so all three paths get it. It's a warning only: exit codes and stdout don't change, so JSON output stays clean.

New tests in `fetch_test.go` cover a remote with no gittuf refs, a remote with only the policy, and a normal remote that gets no warning. Format, lint (0 issues) and `go test -race ./...` all pass. I ran them directly because `mise.toml` still isn't trusted, so `mise run check` won't run.
